I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes to give you yet.

My first request to fetch the sources was refused because the research tool has hit its usage limit. No pages loaded, including the Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, NET Bible notes, Wesley's Notes and Augustine pages for Psalm 56. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from memory, so I haven't written any verse notes.

If you send the request again once the tool is available, I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-56/, and the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* pages for Psalms 56 on biblehub.com.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes on studylight.org (Methodist), plus sermons on vv. 3–4, 8 and 12 from spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, ligonier.org and 1517.org.
- **Other views:**
  - Modern scholarship: the NET Bible notes on the title phrase "A Dove on Distant Oaks," the "bottle" of tears in v. 8 and the vows in v. 12.
  - Catholic: Augustine's commentary on the Psalms on newadvent.org. His Bible numbers this psalm 55, so the page is newadvent.org/fathers/1801055.htm.

You could also paste in text from any of these pages, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from that, with URLs.
